pages.text: Your people belong to $(thing)cultures$(0), each shaped by the climate it calls home. A culture decides the food, dress and comforts its people expect, and the ladder of $(thing)social classes$(0) they climb.$(br2)There are six cultures: $(thing)Desert$(0), $(thing)Steppe$(0), $(thing)Temperate$(0), $(thing)Subarctic$(0), $(thing)Mountain$(0) and $(thing)Tropical$(0).$(br2)$(italic)Design in progress — details may change.$(0)

Each culture is bound to its $(thing)environment$(0). A citizen has standing needs for the right $(thing)altitude$(0), $(thing)temperature$(0) and $(thing)rainfall$(0) — a Desert people wants heat and dry air; a Subarctic one wants the cold. Settle a culture where it belongs, or its people will never be content.$(br2)Within a culture, citizens follow $(thing)vocations$(0) — the culture-specific trades that colour the middle of the class ladder before it converges on a shared elite.

A culture's ladder forms a $(thing)diamond$(0): everyone starts in a common newcomer class, branches into two or three vocations as they prosper, then the most successful reconverge into rare elite and pinnacle classes.$(br2)Crucially, class is $(thing)not$(0) tied to your tech era. It measures $(thing)wealth and comfort$(0), so even a stone-age settlement can raise elites — it just takes patient, labour-intensive luxuries.
